title: Local derived completeness and completed tensor on the canonical small site model
statement: Let $\mathcal S$ be a site, with independent object and morphism universes, essentially small relative to a coefficient universe, and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings. Write $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ for its module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $e:\mathcal S\simeq\mathcal S_0$ be the canonical small-model equivalence with induced topology, and put $R_0=e^{-1,*}R$. Restriction transports global sections of $R$ to $R_0$, and induces the module equivalence $E:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R_0)$ and its exact derived equivalence $D(E):D(R)\simeq D(R_0)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; the two derived morphism universes are independent. For an ideal mono $\iota:I\to R_0$, define $\mathcal C(M)$ to mean that $D(E)(M)$ is locally derived $I$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete], namely that on every slice its derived internal Hom from localization at every local section of $I$ vanishes. For the specified K-flat derived tensor $T:D(R)\times D(R)\to D(R)$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] and a supplied functor $L:D(R)\to\mathcal C$, where $\mathcal C$ is the full subcategory of objects satisfying this predicate, define the completed tensor $B=(\mathcal C\hookrightarrow D(R))^{\times2}\mathbin{\circ}T\mathbin{\circ}L$, in diagrammatic composition order: $B(M,N)=L(T(M,N))$ and $B(f,g)=L(T(f,g))$. In particular this applies when $L$ is a Koszul completion reflector; this definition makes no choice of such a reflector.
